identity.name: Mike Portnoy
identity.summary: Dream Theater's founding drummer, from Berklee in 1985 to 2010 and again from 2023: Neil Peart's odd meters and composed parts on a huge kit, played with a metal drummer's two bass drums. Open hats or the ride over a plain 2 and 4 while the feet run sixteenths; the snare moved onto the "and"s or onto every eighth with the kick between; bars of 5/8, 7/8 and 6/4 dropped into a song as the riff turns; and the hands-and-feet figure named after him, two on the snare, two on the kick. Pull Me Under, Metropolis Part I, The Dance of Eternity, Panic Attack. 'The most important tool is the mind!'

institutions.name: Berklee College of Music
institutions.outcome: A scholarship, 1985; there he met John Petrucci and John Myung and formed Majesty, which became Dream Theater.

traditions.tradition: British and American rock: Ringo, Moon, Bonham and Peter Criss
traditions.impact: 'I cut my teeth on Ringo, Keith Moon, John Bonham, and Peter Criss to learn the basics of the drumkit.'
Neil Peart's odd meters, learned by playing along ('That's how I learned to play in odd meters'); Bill Bruford's odd meters and long compositions.
'My application of double bass drumming within Dream Theater comes more from my metal side': Lars Ulrich, Charlie Benante.

formative_events.event: Went to Berklee on a scholarship; met John Petrucci and John Myung and formed Majesty, renamed Dream Theater.
Images and Words and Pull Me Under, a top-ten rock radio hit.
Left Dream Theater in September after 25 years; played Nightmare with Avenged Sevenfold.
Rejoined Dream Theater, announced 25 October, in place of Mike Mangini.

eras.label: Images and Words and Awake
eras.context: With Kevin Moore on keyboards, under outside producers: David Prater's triggered kick and snare on Images and Words, then Awake's darker, heavier songs.
defining_traits: double bass under a plain backbeat
toms as the groove (Metropolis Part I)

eras.label: Scenes from a Memory to Black Clouds & Silver Linings
eras.context: Producing the band himself with John Petrucci, Jordan Rudess on keyboards: the concept records, the heaviest riffs and the longest songs.
defining_traits: a new meter every bar (The Dance of Eternity)

eras.label: The return
eras.context: Back in the band after thirteen years, Parasomnia produced by Petrucci.

swing.notes: Straight sixteenths throughout; the meters, not a swing, are the feel.

dynamics.balance: Loud and even; no ghost notes in the tabs read; the china and crashes for the accents.

feel_profile.interaction: Set to the riff: the kick and cymbals with the guitar and keyboard unisons, the meter turning when the riff does.

hand_techniques.name: the snare off the backbeat
hand_techniques.description: The snare on every "and" (Pull Me Under's interlude), on every eighth with the kick between (its second pre-chorus), or moved onto the "e" of 3 and the "a" of 4 (Home).

hand_techniques.name: the ride and hats in turn
hand_techniques.description: As I Am's chorus in 7/8: the ride on the eighths, the hats on the sixteenths between.

hand_techniques.name: toms as the groove
hand_techniques.description: Metropolis Part I's verse on the mid tom, Pull Me Under's intro on the floor tom, The Dance of Eternity's floor tom in fives.

foot_techniques.name: double bass in sixteenths
foot_techniques.description: Two bass drums running sixteenths under a plain backbeat or a china on the beat (Pull Me Under's pre-chorus, Night Terror's riff); 'from my metal side'.

foot_techniques.name: hands and feet in turn
foot_techniques.description: The 'Portnoy fill': two sixteenths on the snare or a tom, two on the bass drums, repeated (Wikipedia); Metropolis Part I's verse 2 plays it as a groove, and Panic Attack's intro in threes, a hand and two feet.

foot_techniques.name: the hat foot on the off-beats
foot_techniques.description: The hat foot on the "e" of every beat under hats on the beat (Metropolis Part I and Home).

devices.description: Panic Attack's intro: the snare and a china every three sixteenths with two kicks between, a hand and two feet, grouped 3+3+3+3+2+2 across the 4/4 bar.
The Dance of Eternity's djent riff: the floor tom in groups of five sixteenths (four and a rest) with the guitars, across bars of 5/4 and 6/4.

searched: The nine Songsterr tabs read section by section (Pull Me Under to Night Terror), and The Glass Prison (5555) read and not used
Wikipedia (the 'Portnoy fill', credited to Terry Bozzio: hands and feet in turn, not a cross-rhythm)
Modern Drummer's 2007 interview (its opening) and Far Out's 2023 list of his favourites
devices_search.note: Two groupings found in the tabs, both in the groove. The meter changes (6/4 and 5/8 by turns, 7/8 dropped into 4/4) are written as sections in their own meters, not as devices. The Metropolis breakdown's tempo, half again the instrumental's, may be a metric modulation; not sourced, so not claimed.

voice_language.snare: The backbeat plain and loud; moved onto the "and"s or onto every eighth; runs of sixteenths into a section.
voice_language.kick: Two bass drums: sixteenths under the riff, pairs on the "and" and "a", or with the guitar's rhythm.
voice_language.toms: The groove itself in places (Metropolis Part I, Pull Me Under's intro); fills down the toms at a phrase's end.
voice_language.hihat: Open in eighths over the verse; on the beat with the hat foot between.
voice_language.ride: In eighths over double bass; the bell for a chorus.
voice_language.cymbals: A china on every beat or every "and"; splashes for the accents; the crash ridden in quarters or eighths.

aesthetic: a huge kit, two bass drums, many cymbals and a china
a big, processed sound on Images and Words; heavier and tighter after
sound_profile.cymbal_character: Sabian: crashes, two chinas, Max Stax (a china stacked on a splash or crash), splashes and bell chimes round him (Sabian's artist page).

by_era.description: Images and Words' kick and snare triggered from samples by the producer, in a big reverb.
A metal kit, punchy and tight, the cymbals big.

sample_hints.1994-2025: Crocell: a metal band's kit, a punchy kick and a cracking snare, big cymbals.

signature_traits.label: Meters that change with the riff
signature_traits.description: Bars of 5/8, 7/8, 6/4 and 9/8 dropped into a song, the groove kept whole through each.

signature_traits.label: Double bass under a plain backbeat
signature_traits.description: Two bass drums in sixteenths under the snare on 2 and 4, or on every beat under a china.

signature_traits.label: Hands and feet in turn
signature_traits.description: Two on the snare, two on the kick (the 'Portnoy fill'), or a hand and two feet in threes.

signature_traits.label: A china on the beat
signature_traits.description: The china ridden on every beat or every "and" over the riff.

patterns.function: Hats in eighths, the last one open, the snare on the "and" of 2, the kick on 1, the "a" of 1 and the "e" of 2

patterns.function: A china on every beat, the kick pushed onto the "and" of 1, 3, its "and" and the "and" of 4

philosophy.idea: Learn odd meters by playing along with the records that use them, as he learned Rush.
Progressive means a willingness to experiment and keep an open mind; the most important tool is the mind.

innovations: Progressive metal drumming: Peart's odd meters and composed parts with a metal drummer's double bass, on records from Images and Words on

cultural_references.description: Thirty-two Modern Drummer awards; the Modern Drummer Hall of Fame at 37, the second-youngest after Neil Peart.
Panic Attack, in Rock Band 2, the game's hardest song on the drums.

common_misconceptions: That his odd meters are a jazz drummer's: by his own account they came from Rush and Yes, and the double bass from metal.
